newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures finish higher in quiet trading.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures finish higher in quiet trading.

text.p: U.S. debt futures finished higher in quiet trading, recovering from an early test of support in December Treasury bonds.

December T-bonds dipped early to 110-00 after a stronger than expected durable goods orders report for September, then recovered as dealer buying kicked in near the session lows. A weaker than expected September existing home sales figure later in the morning helped boost T-bond futures into the key 111-00 handle. Trade was light late.
Despite the recovery, futures traders said the market ended neutral for the week.
"In the beginning of the week they ground it down and then you just worked your way back to the middle of the range," a T-bond options trader said.
Another trader noted that even though December T-bonds clearly rejected the week's lows, it would have taken a close above 111-13/32 to turn the mood bullish.
"It was quiet trading and we're not even back to the middle of the week's range," he said.
In the short end, March Eurodollar futures were still stuck in the recent 94.26 to 94.35 range.

"Euros got sold late in the day, but other than that it was pretty quiet," a Euro broker said. He said two firms together sold about 3,000 March contracts in the last two minutes of trade at 94.32, 94.31 and 94.30.
March Euros closed up two basis points at 94.31.

Early in the session, it was reported that September durable goods rose 4.6 percent overall and 4.5 percent excluding the defense sector, but gained only 0.9 percent excluding transportation orders. September existing home sales fell 2.9 percent to a 4.02 million annual rate from a revised 4.14 million rate in August.

At settlement, 10-year notes were up 6/32 at 108-16/32, muni-bonds gained 12/32 to 114-11/32 and March T-bills rose one basis point to 94.82. -Derivatives Desk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
